notes.title: Star Fleet II V2.0.17
notes.content:
[p]Hey friends, long time no see! We're here with another update for this lovely game, the details of which you can see below directly from Dr. Sorenson! Thanks for being awesome, and please continue to enjoy the game!

Version Number: 2.0.17
Date: September 15, 2025

Introduction:
Some new features and some bug fixes.

Additions/Improvements/Changes:
1. When a planet is destroyed (annihilated) by obliterator pods or a super nova, it is retained in the planet databases, although it is designated as having been destroyed.
2. There is a new shortcut to view the landing parties database and a couple resultant changes in the shortcuts. Here are the new designations:

- [Alt]\[K]: shortcut to landing parties database (was previously the message box retention switch for the star maps)
- [Ctrl]\[M]: message box retention in star maps switch (was previously \[Alt]\[K])
- [Ctrl]\[P]: performance mode toggle switch (was previously \[Ctrl]\[M])

3. A dynamic indicator has been added to the Tactical Display that shows when a ship has jumped into hyperspace. Note that this occurs at its new jump position, which is not exactly the same as the previous plotted position in the Tactical Display. This was added per a suggestion of a player.
4. Several new topics have been added to the Ship Information System (SIS), i.e., the ship's onboard Wiki.

Fixes:
1. Fixed formatting error in TARGET DISPLAY when orbit status changed.
2. When Help requested from KHQ, got response "No help available" when help was actually ordered - fixed.
3. When a lower rank presses \[I] in Fleet Command, you get a "FUNCTION NOT AVAILABLE AT THIS RANK" message that results in an endless loop - fixed.
4. On the Landing Parties database, selecting detailed status of a LP on the second page shows the detailed status of the corresponding LP on the first page - fixed
\[/I]\[/P][/p][/*][/olist]

notes.title: Star Fleet II 2.0.15 Released!
notes.content:
STAR FLEET II VERSION 2 PATCH NOTES
Version Number: 2.0.14
Date: March 18, 2024

Introduction:
This was a test version.

Additions/Improvements/Changes:
1. In the Orbital Display, when the Science/Scanners option is selected, the Description Box for the object in the Target Designator Box (TDB) will also show the orbital position of the object if it is a Krellan ship, UGA ship, or Orbital Fort (but not your escorts). The orbital position has the format "O:" that shows the orbit type ("H", "M", or "L" for High, Medium, or Low orbits respectively) followed by the position in that orbit ("P:"). The zero position for each orbit is at the bottom of the planet and increments in a CW direction.
2. This same orbital position format is now used in the TARGET DATA display when in orbit. The orbit type is replaced by the letter instead of the numbers 0, 1, 2 (high, medium, low). 
3. In the Fleet Maintenance (login Fleet/Manager), the Service Record (SrvRcd) maintenance is now partially functional. You can list the Service Record which shows the values for each entry in the record along with its meaning. You can select [All] to view the entire Service Record file or you can select a player number to view the record for only that player. You can also select the Modify Option, which partially works. You first select the player whose record you want to modify (from the Fleet Personnel list), then select the entry you want to change. You will be prompted for the new value or just press [Enter] to leave it unchanged. There is an option [A] to look at the list of awards so you can determine the correct number corresponding to each award. Currently, only the initial screen of records can be shown in the Modify option ([PgDn] and [PgUp] don't work yet). In this version, any changes you make are not kept.


Fixes:
None

=======================================================================================================
Version Number: 2.0.15
Date: April 8, 2024

Introduction:
This is a test version.

Additions/Improvements/Changes:
None

Fixes:
1. When trying to beam up your Landing Party (LP) from a planet with a base that has extra crew and shock troops, instead of just your selected Landing Parties beaming up, all the Krellan personnel on the planet beam up - FIXED
2. If there is a LP on a planet, then you are unable to use the Personnel Transfer in Teleporters to beam up personnel not in your LP - FIXED
3.Orbiting a planet with a base, Personnel Transfer will beam captives to the planet and doesn't allow personnel transfer - FIXED.
4. Took steps to reduce the possibility of getting system errors being reported from Engineering.

notes.title: Star Fleet II 2.0.9 and 2.1.0
notes.content:
STAR FLEET II VERSION 2 PATCH NOTES
Version Number: 2.0.9
Date: January 9, 2024

Introduction:
This is a test version.

Additions/Improvements/Changes:
1. Career Statistic Display was unable to handle some large numbers, such as Booty or Fines. It also had problems displaying large numbers which could overflow the space available. The table has been enlarged to handle larger numbers, and the Career Statistics file has been changed to handle larger numbers. For Example, the total number of Krels obtained in Booty was limited to 65,535. If there were more Krels than that, it would show a negative number. I've changed the critical numbers so their upper limit is over 1 million. This means the old career statistics files are no longer compatible with the game. When you log on, it checks to see if you have the new stats file or the old one. If the old one, it will automatically convert it to the new one and you will get a message that the career stats file is being converted. From then on it should be no problem. During the conversion, if it comes across a number that is negative because it's too large, it will convert it to the maximum size of 65,535.


Fixes:
1. When bombarding a planet with your escorts and you change their Targeting orders from Bombard to something else (other than Hold Fire), although they will stop hitting the planet, they will still be using torps like they were firing. - FIXED
2. An Escort can sometimes lose it's name. If this happens, call up the Escorts orders (Alt+Z) and a new name will be assigned to the escort. Immediately save the game so the name is permanently attached.
3. OBB Status Box cannot handle OpET values >=10 or the number overwrites the allocated space - FIXED
4. OBB was started with a Krellan base on the planet (there cannot be a base there for OBB) - FIXED
5. While OBB was underway, it was possible to beam LP down to the planet (not allowed) - FIXED

notes.title: STAR FLEET II 2.0.5-2.0.8
notes.content:
STAR FLEET II VERSION 2 PATCH NOTES
Version Number: 2.0.5
Date: December 27, 2023

Introduction:
Several bugs have been fixed, but I am still working on others. A couple of new features or changes have also been made.

Additions/Improvements/Changes:
1. When the XO asks if you want to board an enemy ship after it surrendered, you no longer have to select the ship after answering "Y". The XO and your crew know which ship it is.
2. "Blinky" now uses his full name, "Blinky Bill".
3. When you go to Alignment Mode (Alt+O while not moving in normal space), the mode will show "ALIGNMNT" to remind you that you are in this special static mode. I have also redefined the colors of some of the modes.
4. In the Planetary Invasion module, I've added a warning that if you attempt to quit before the invasion is complete the invasion will be considered a failure and all your legions involved in the invasion will be lost. It then suggests that if you want to temporarily quit, you should save the game and then exit to DOS (Ctrl+X).


Fixes:
1. In Practice Mode it goes straight to Sign-On Options after the Mission Tally instead of giving you the chance to delete files - FIXED
2. In information displayed to a new cadet, "manual" was misspelled as "manaual" - FIXED
3. When standard probes are detonated from Engineering (i.e., while on the Bridge Display), part of the Launch Control box remained on top of the Bridge Display when you exited Launch Control - FIXED
4. Deleting files from End of Mission and from Resume Game option not being handled properly - FIXED
5. There was a Gaseous (G class) planet in Krellan space that had a Krellan base on it and was listed as being a Krellan Planet (but had no personnel). No G-class planet should have a base on it - FIXED
6. After a successful invasion, the troopships have no drop ships - FIXED
7. From Resume Game option in Sign-on Options, it was not possible to delete saved invasions - FIXED
8. The information option in the Battlecruiser selection display was out of date (stated you needed to be Subadmiral instead of Prefect for upgrade) - FIXED
9. Captives beamed up from planet not counted in Mission Tally - FIXED

notes.title: Star Fleet II 2.0.3 and 2.0.4
notes.content:
STAR FLEET II VERSION 2 PATCH NOTES
Version Number: 2.0.3
Date: December 5, 2023

Introduction:
Several bugs have been fixed, still working on others.

Additions/Improvements:
1. Some tweaks were made to the AI.

Fixes:
1. Captives brought back by the Boarding Party were disappearing shortly after being taken to Security. FIXED
2. When initiating a patrol before fully emerged from hyperspace, game was freezing. FIXED - you cannot initiate a Search or Patrol until you have fully emerged from hyperspace.
3. You cannot downgrade from RED ALERT if a threat is detected. FIXED - you can now downgrade from RED ALERT even if there is a threat as long as the AAS is switched to manual.
4. In the Career Statistics Display, if the total for Passengers or Captives exceeds 65565, then the number was wrong - FIXED
5. In orbit of a planet in the same system as a colony, torps fired at an orbital target would hit an Orb Fort (but causing no damage), which was orbiting the colony and not the planet your ship is orbiting. FIXED
6. A couple other minor or secret (i.e., items not revealed to the player) bugs were fixed.

=============================================================

Version Number: 2.0.4
Date: December 10, 2023

Introduction:
Version 2.0.3 was a test version only and not released to the user community.

Additions/Improvements:
1. A new Hot Key shortcut has been added for the Performance Mode. This switches between two methods of writing some data to the screen, using either DOS functions or the BIOS functions. One is slower (NORMAL Mode) than the other (TURBO Mode). The default value is TURBO Mode, but some players want to slow combat down and like to temporarily switch it to NORMAL Mode. This can be done through the Settings Panel in the Sign-On Options ("C" - change settings) or in the game itself by accessing the same panel through the Computer/Special Services. This takes time to do and is a bit clumsy, so the new shortcut has been added: [Ctrl][M] (for Mode). It can also now be changed through the Hot Keys command [Ctrl][H]. You can see the current setting of the switch in Engineering/Engineering Data/Logistics.
2. An enhancement has been made to upgraded probes. In the Operations table, you could view the location of the probe currently highlighted, or you could use the multi-probe selection feature to view the location of multiple probes. There is now the option to view the location of ALL the probes. If you select [S]how locn without multiple probes being selected, it will ask you if you want to view the locations of all the probes. If "Y" then the Ops Table disappear and you will see the locations of the probes. A new feature added for this and multiple-probes option is that the color of the probes will match their mode as displayed in the Ops Table. Destroyed (by any means) probes are also now included (all in red). There is also a shortcut for viewing all the probes. Press [Shift][S] instead of just [S] from the probes menu.

Fixes:
1. In the Boarding Display after the enemy ship has been captured, the number of captives taken did not include the Space Marines and thus did not match the number of captives transported to your ship - FIXED
2. When you have the LOW SUP warning, captives are not fed and gradully die off, but they were not dying fast enough. Also, if you went to secuirty during this time, the captives health could be shown as "good" instead of "poor" - FIXED
3. Killed captives from LOW SUP or LOW POW (when all the remaining captives are killed) or normal execution does not update the Mission Tally - FIXED
4.The message from a supply ship that it is running low on cargo and headed to another supply ship did not include the name of the target ship - FIXED
5. Ship could downgrade from RED ALERT and drop shields when going into orbit around a UGA planet - FIXED
6. Setup for Mission 3-E modified to ensure there are at least 4 planets that can be bombarded into submission.
7. When orbiting a hostile TL5+ planet that has bot been surveyed and you send a message demanding it surrender, it would respond with an insult message, even though it was unsruveyed. It will now not respond (with a possible rare exception) - FIXED

notes.title: Star Fleet II 2.02
notes.content:
STAR FLEET II VERSION 2 PATCH NOTES
Version Number: 2.0.02
Date: 11/23/2023

Introduction:
A few bugs have been fixed. Some improvements in instructions for new cadets have been made.

Additions/Improvements:
1. When a new recruit signs on, they are told to read the Training Manual before starting a mission.
2. Turorials no longer show the Mission Orders, and they are not accessible within the game to avoid confusion. The Career page is also not available. Trying to access orders results in an error that can be ignored, and this will be fixed in the next patch.

Fixes:
1. When you change the pitch of the engine sound using Ctrl+E, the new frequency is now saved and used. Previously it was being lost.
2. Detonating a probe from a star map while it was in flight messed up the Launch Control display. FIXED
3. In Material Transfer if the target had negative power, it showed as infinity instead of zero. FIXED
4. In the Command Tree for Computer/Special Services, the "Quit" command highlight was one row off. FIXED
5. If you run out of energy or low on supplies, the captives weren't being killed off (Please note, killed captives aren't being added to the mission tally, this will be fixed in the next patch). FIXED 
6. Brian Rubin here, I forgot to add two types of files to Steam cloud saving, .log for log files and .npd for notepad files, but they've been added and should now sync properly. Sorry about that. Thanks to Wahnsinniger on Steam for helping with this one.

notes.title: SF2 V2.0 Beta.39
notes.content:
STAR FLEET II VERSION 2 PATCH NOTES
Version Number: Beta.39
Date: 11/10/2023

Introduction:
This patch makes a couple minor adjustments and fixes one bug.

Additions/Improvements:
1. The threshold level for the LOW PWR and LOW SUP warnings has been modified to be 25% of maximum level instead of a set quantity, which would make it 20% each for both warnings for the upgraded battlecruiser (Flagship). This makes it consistent with the documentation.
2. When you get the LOW PWR warning and you are not at RED ALERT status, then the XO will lower your shields to save power, regardless of the setting of the AAS.

Fixes:
1. Escorts were unable to dock with a captured starbase when initially asked to do so. They could dock later with a Rendezvous command. Fixed - they will now dock initially.

notes.title: A Quick Update
notes.content:
Hey friends, 

Brian Rubin here! I've been getting some questions as to how the game is coming along so I wanted to chime in and give y'all a quick update! So far here's what's going on:

[b]Delays:[/b]

Some real-life stuff has delayed us a bit, such as Trevor's floppy drive failing (he still programs the game on his 486) plus some deadlines he had for his other work at Interstel, such as satellite contracts! Those have pretty much passed, and the floppy drive is working again, so we're back on track.

[b]What's Done:[/b]

The code audit is complete, which was a huge deal, and has made the game much more stable. 

[b]What's Currently Being Worked On:[/b]

Right now much of the work is focusing on the documentation, as much of it has needed to be updated, but we're not far from being done on that. We've also made progress on the training manual as well. We're also working on a new trailer for the game

[b]The State of the Game:[/b]

The current beta has been pretty rock solid. I've gotten some time with it and have had no bugs, and none of the other playtesters have reported any for a while, so the game feels as close as it's ever been to being complete.

[b]Final Thoughts:[/b]

Only one person wants to get this game in your hands more than me, and that's Trevor himself. We're all working hard to get this game to you, but we want to do it right. I want to, again, thank you all for your patience and excitement for this game. 

Thanks for reading this quick update, and again for your patience. Y'all are the best.

Stay tuned, we'll have more soon!

notes.title: We've Hit Beta!!
notes.content:
Friends, Brian Rubin here with an update! We've been quiet a bit lately, but that doesn't mean nothing has happened. I have the distinct pleasure of telling y'all that today, we finally hit beta. Now a number of things will happen to bring it to launch, including:

[list]
[*] More Bug Fixing
[*] A Code Audit
[*] Updated Documentation
[/list]
And likely a lot more. We're now, likely, only a couple of months away from finally releasing the game! I cannot WAIT y'all! Stay tuned!!

notes.title: A Quick Update
notes.content:
Friends, Brian Rubin here, and I just wanted to give you a quick update on how things are going with Star Fleet II 2.0! Work is still on going, but some things have admittedly slowed us down, such as:

[olist]
[*]Trevor -- the lone developer -- not only had to finish up his semester of teaching along with other rocket scientist work, but he was also recently injured in his leg (nothing super major, thankfullly), which has slowed him down. He's recovering nicely, thank goodness, but it's obviously slowed things down a touch.
[*]This one is my fault. We've been tweaking the last few missions of the game to make them, hopefully, better balanced. I've been banging my head against the penultimate mission for almost a year now, but I'm FINALLY close to finishing it. Sadly, something with my save game has been bugged, so Trevor has been working to fix it.  This has resulted in bugs fixed in the program itself as well, but of course it's taken time.
[/olist]
On the other hand, work on the game has been continuing. Many internal versions have been released, and we are THIS close to beta, when we lock down all new features and focused solely on bug hunting and fixing, as well as a code audit.

Oh, we also finally got accepted onto [url=https://www.gog.com/en/game/star_fleet_ii_krellan_commander_version_20]GOG[/url]! Yay! We'll be happy no matter where you buy the game, so wishlist it wherever you like, please and thank you. ;)

We've also begun work on some other things like a new trailer and updated documentation as well! 

So,  work HAS been happening, it's just we've all been too busy (me especially) to post about it, so I apologize for that. Please be sure we want to get the game to you as SOON as possible, we just want to do it right. The last thing we want, as I've said before, is a repeat of the problematic (and I'm being kind) 1.0 launch from 1989. 

I, therefore, want to thank you for your continued patience and excitement for this game. My excitement for this game hasn't waned even though I've probably put in around 1,000 hours into it at this point, and I cannot WAIT to get it to you.

Thanks again for your patience, and please don't hesitate to ask any questions if you have them. See you soon with more info!

notes.title: Starfleet II Development Update - 3/5/22
notes.content:
My friends, Brian Rubin here, again coming to you with an apology for the lateness of this. Life has just been hectic as well, and getting Covid back in January DEFINITELY slowed me down, but now things have gotten to a point wherein I can put this dang dev update together for you all!

A lot has happened since our last update. The final big feature of 2.0 -- the captain's log, which integrates all the log files into a chronological, readable story about your mission -- is in, and currently being worked on, and we feel now we're just a few months away from releasing this thing into your grubby paws. On a personal note I just passed 100 episodes streamed of Star Fleet II, which has equaled roughly 250 hours of campaign play. This game is huge y'all.

Alright, without further adieu, here are the latest updates -- which include new features -- up to today, 3/5/22. Please note, pure bug fix releases were not included:

[list]
[*] 11/19/21 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R_09.txt]Version 1.9 Release 0.9[/url] - Updates to how invasions are handled and displayed.
[*]11/29/21 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R_101.txt]Version 1.9 Release 1.01[/url] - New indicator for planetary government types (unified/not unified) and lots of bug fixes. 
[*]12/6/21 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R_103.txt]Version 1.9 Release 1.03[/url] - Updated line of sight priority for targets in orbit that are in LOS, along with bug fixes.
[*]12/16/21 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R_104.txt]Version 1.9 Release 1.04[/url] - Expanded XO role, updated engine schematic, freighter power indicators and more, along with bug fixes.
[*]1/9/22 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R_111.txt]Version 1.9 Release 1.11[/url] - The first iteration of the new Ship Information System, or SIS, has been implemented. This is an in-game reference library in which you can search for any number of topics, from torpedoes to boarding and everything in-between. We've been fleshing this out as we go and it is turning into something awesome. Eventually, it'll be a full in-game manual and wiki of sorts, we hope. This plus plenty of bug fixes.
[*]2/18/22 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R1_22.TXT]Version 1.9 Release 1.22[/url] - The big one here is invasions. Whereas before, remote (AI-led) invasions would take several days, but now that take far less time to be more in-line with human-led invasions. This will be a massive boon in later, Admiral-level missions. 
[*]2/19/22 -[url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R1_23.TXT]Version 1.9 Release 1.23[/url] - More invasion-specific updates for this one. Now your XO will inform you when a remote invasion (AI-led) has begun, the strategic invasion display now shows cities captured or destroyed, and if more than half are invaded or destroyed, the planet may now surrender. 
[*]2/20/22 -[url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R1_24.TXT]Version 1.9 Release 1.24[/url] - The big one here is some probe-related QOL features, such as showing how many probes you have in the launch tubes and how many you have in storage, which is VERY helpful let me tell you.
[*]2/22/22 - [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R1_25.TXT]Version 1.9 Release 1.25[/url] - Some QOL features regarding both landing parties and remote destroyers when they discover enemies in a system.
[/list]
We've also had a lot of bug fix releases as well, which brings us up to v1.9 release 1.27 as of today. The next release should be 1.9 release 2.0, which might add some new stuff and should be coming within days. 

We now hope to have the game ready to release to you in a couple of months. Some things we still need to do, besides working on the game itself, is:

[list]
[*] Revise and update the documentation.
[*] Further update the Steam page with more new features.
[*] Come up with a new trailer for the game.
[/list]
I feel like we're truly in the home stretch y'all. Thank you so much for your patience with us. We definitely want to bring you the most feature-complete and bug-free version of the game that we can. I'll try to do the next update in a more timely manner, and maybe that'll be the last one before release! Yay!

Thanks for reading, my friends, and please let us know if you have any questions. Be safe and well!

notes.title: Star Fleet II Development Update - 11/17/21
notes.content:
My friends, welcome to the latest Star Fleet II Development Update. First off, let me apologize at the long amount of time between the last one and this one. Life kept getting busier and busier and I just never set aside the time to pound this out. I'm going to try to do this in little bits in the future so it won't be some massive thing in my mind, and therefore easy to avoid. If I chip away at it bit by bit, it'll be easier for me to get these to you.

Anyway enough about that, you're here to learn about what's been going on with Star Fleet II! The big word is: Probes. In recent updates, Trevor has added an entirely new way to use probes for Subadmirals and Admirals. Whereas before this new update, probes would go to a system, passively tell you what might be there in terms of planets, enemies, and starbases, and that was pretty much it.

Now, probes have an active mode that not only lets them go into orbit and scan planets, but also searches systems for enemy Starbases. It makes the exploration part of a mission MUCH more streamlined. That isn't to say it makes the game EASIER. Far from it. The probes help you find stuff more quickly, but you still need to deal with said stuff once you find it. Finding a UGA colony only a day or two into a mission does not make it any less of a challenge to deal with. 

There have been a TON of other updates and fixes as well, and you'll be able to read all about them in the release notes linked below (I'm sorry I don't have approximate dates for these). These are all for version 1.9. 

[list]
[*] Release 0.6 - Nav will check to see if there's a black hole in your path upon choosing a new navigational target. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R06.txt]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.7 - New Probes Systems for Subadmirals and Admirals. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R07.TXT]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.71-0.73 - Exploring probes will optimize their routes more effectively to save energy. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R073.TXT]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.80 - Changed the color of colonies in the planets table for easier identification. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R08.TXT]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.81 - Starforts will now be more spread apart. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/RNWS9081.TXT]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.82/0.83 - Supply ships will now give updates on their ETA if requested again. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/RNWS9083.TXT]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.84 - Probes are now color-coded in the Probe Operations Control depending on their energy level. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/RNWS9084.TXT]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[*] Release 0.86 - You'll now be asked if you wish to have a Destroyer explore a system if it thinks there are enemies there. [url=https://starfleet2.com/files/R086.txt]Full Notes Here.[/url]
[/list]
Now that the new Probe Operations Control is up and running, the next big feature Trevor plans to implement before 2.0 is the Captain's Log, which will be a personal journal of the captain. This will then be rolled into an all-encompassing Mission Log. This fully-integrated Mission Log will combine the Report Log, Message Log AND Captain's Log into one chronological document that details what happened during a mission. This is the final thing Trevor really wants to implement into the game before 2.0 finally launches, but it also might happen after 2.0 hits. We're not entirely sure yet. 

Regardless, this means we still don't have a final release date for the game, but it's looking less likely to be 2021. I'd reckon, at the rate things are happening, Q1, 2022 is far more likely. Please understand that we need to take the time to get this as stable, bug-free and well-documented as possible before releases, and we're all working hard, Trevor and playtesters like, to make that happen. We truly appreciate and thank you for your patience.

With that said, I hope you've enjoyed this development update, and I hope to catch you here on Steam, or YouTube or Twitch, every Monday morning for more Star Fleet II. Thanks for reading, and don't hesitate to hit us up if you have any questions. 

P.S. Don't forget, we're still actively looking for playtesters, as the more folks helping us find bugs, the quicker this will get released. Be sure to [url=https://starfleet2.com/contact/]contact us[/url] if you have the time and interest, and thank you.

notes.title: July/August, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.content:
Hey friends, Brian Rubin here, and happy September! Sorry for the delay in this, I had a VERY busy July and August, to the point wherein only now are things slowing down and I have time to update y'all on the latest stuff going on with Star Fleet II!

First off, I wanna talk about release dates. Recently we pushed it back to October, but I'm gonna be honest, with the work that still remains, I'm not sure we'll be ready for October. This is not only due to the work that remains, but the fact that Trevor also basically has two other jobs: College Professor and Rocket Scientist, and September is going to be busy with both. So from now on, no release dates. We're gonna stick with "When it's ready" and hopefully get it out well before the end of the year, but again, we also want to do this right. We want to get the game to where Trevor wants it, feature-wise, and then work to get it as bug-free as possible for launch, as well as updating the necessary documentation. So while I'd LOVE for us to get it out in October, please understand if it's a smidge later than that.

Now, with that all said, let's get to the actual updates! We're now internally testing 1.9, which already has a ton of new features, such as armed freighters, a conditional firing mode that'll try to destroy warships and disable freighters and starliners, and some new toys in the Krellan arsenal. Here are the highlights, along with a download of the text file with all the updates for each version and release number. Please note, these should be opened in Wordpad. Now let's dive in, shall we?

[h2]Update Hightlights and Version Text File Downloads[/h2]

[h3]Version 1.8[/h3]

[list]
[*]version 1.8 release 0.6 - A minor one, Circuit was changed to Patrol in the helm commands, plus several bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS0.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r1.1 - This one gives you an option to do an emergency stop if hit by a mine, or to keep going, plus other bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS1.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v.1.8 r1.3 - This one adds a feature to set personnel transfer to the standard amount of crew for a prize crew of a captured ship automatically, plus numerous bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS2.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r1.4 - The big change here is that the default status for newly-captured enemies is now "Question" rather than "Hold", which can be a good and bad thing. ;) This plus numerous bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS3.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r1.5 - This one was entirely done to fix some bugs. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS4.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r1.6 - Another purely bug-fixing release. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS5.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r2.0 - This one adds numerous features, such as the invade command to Fleet Command, along with a new command called disperse, which will force all current local forces to disperse around your ship to about ten sectors. This is great for quick resupplies right before attacking a starbase or orbital forts, and also is great for spreading out your fleet just before such an attack so fewer are hit by mines. Planetary invasions also got some love, as now you can easily see how many surface-to-air lasers and planetary-defense-phasers a zone has, so you can focus on taking them out if need be. Your XO will now also ask you if you want to set your weapons to disable when attacking a freighter or starliner. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS6.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r2.1 & 2.2 - This one adds a new visual indicator so you can quickly see if your escorts are resupplied in a starfort and all ready to go. Supply ships will now also restock crew and marines as well as supplies. Also, color coding has now been added to the data box so you can see at a glance if anything is in dire need of attention. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS7.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r2.3 - A purely big fix release. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS8.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.8 r2.4 - This one adds more information as to where suspected starbases might be lurking to the intelligence screen, along with some bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNEWS9.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[/list]

[h3]Version 1.9[/h3]

[list]
[*]version 1.9 release 0.1 - Version 1.9 adds a host of new features, such as new Krellan toys like the Klink Drive (a reverse-engineered version of the Blink Drive artifact, which lets you jump anywhere on the map) and the Nova Bomb (which was in a testing phase in this release), which can cause a system's sun to go nova. UGA freighters and Krellan troopships now have a single phaser for defense, and planetary defense for UGA colonies has been improved, sadly. ;) This is a big one y'all. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNWS5.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.9 r0.2 - Nova Bomb is ready for action, along with some bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNWS6.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.9 r0.3 - For planetary invasions, you can now at a glance see the number of SALs and PDPs in a zone, plus some bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNWS7.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]v1.9 r0.4 - Conditional weapon setting added, which will now default to destroy for warships and disable for freighters and starliners when set in the weapons menu. Krellan-owned planets will now supply both you and your escorts, like a supply ship, plus some big bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNWS8.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[*]1.9 r0.5 - Missions 7-D and 7-D get clearer language for dealing with planets, plus several big bug fixes. [url=https://www.starfleet2.com/files/RLSNWS9.TXT]Download Text File.[/url]
[/list]

That does it for this round of updates! The game is coming along swimmingly and I could NOT be more excited about how it plays now. Every update makes me feel more and more like a proper starship captain/commander, and it's GREAT. I so can't wait to get this into your hands, folks. Thanks for reading, and don't hesitate to hit us up with any questions. Thank you!

notes.title: May (and Kinda June), 2021 Development Update
notes.content:
Friends, first off let me apologize for the lateness of this. Work and life have just been super busy, in a good way really, and I've just not had the time to put this together, so this one is gonna be a bit truncated to save me time, but I'll be linking full version release notes so you can see for yourself how much has improved.

Here's the rundown:

In early May, 1,7 was released and it brought with it a whole bevy of new features. This includes:

[list]
[*]A full career statistics screen that tallies everything from your first mission onward.
[*]New quick navigation options, such as the nearest starbase, or a specific star system or planet from their respective information tables. 
[*]New database options for looking at landing parties and bases.
[*]New status screens for landing parties and Operation Big Brother.
[*]New features to Fleet Command, such as see every ship's distance from you at a glance, or all their objectives.
[*]New escort formations and a formation editor.
[*]Orbital Fortresses, which are basically starbases orbiting UGA colonies.
[*]Qships, warships disguised as freighters
[/list]
1.7 received several patches, the notes to which you can read here:

[list]
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/SF2_V1_7R1.0_Notes.pdf]1.7 Release 1.0 Notes[/url] (PDF)
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/SF2_V1_7R2.0_Notes.pdf]1.7 Release 2.0 Notes[/url] (PDF)
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/NEWS_V1.7R3.0.txt]1.7 Release 3.0 Notes[/url] (TXT)
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/SF2_V1_7R3.1_Notes.pdf]1.7 Release 3.1 Notes[/url] (PDF)
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/SF2_V1_7R4.0_Notes.pdf]1.7 Release 4.0 Notes[/url] (PDF)
[/list]
In late May, 1.8 was released to select playtesters and brings with it even more new features, such as:

[list]
[*]System search, which will now send your fleet in a sweep around a system. Handy for keeping your fleet together and looking for starbases or UGA ships.
[*]Fleet command has received several new commands, such as multi-mode and local mode. Multi-mode allows you to select multiple ships and give them the same order easily. There are also keyboard shortcuts to select all warships, or all ships, or all battlecruisers, and so on. 
[*]Fleet Command local mode only highlights ships in your system for selection, making it easy to only focus on the ships in your immediate vicinity. You can also see where everyone's position is using the new position command. 
[*]As a Subadmiral or Admiral, you can order a moratorium on invasions from Fleet HQ, so that only you can order invasions. This is VERY handy in missions where you goals are planetary invasions. 
[*]A new helm patrol mode, which will do an orbit around a specific object or point in space. Perfect for protecting Starforts. 
[*]Slaves can now be converted to Krells, the game's currency, upon reaching the rank of Prefect. 
[*]Improvements to planetary invasions. 
[/list]
You can see the patch notes here:

[list]
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/NEWS_V1.8R0.1.txt]1.8 Release 0.1 Release Notes[/url] (TXT)
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/NEWS_V1.8R0.2.txt]1.8 Release 0.2 Release Notes[/url] (TXT)
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/NEWS_V1.8R0.3.txt]1.8 Release 0.3 Release Notes[/url] (TXT) 
[*][url=https://starfleet2.com/files/NEWS_V1.8R0.4.txt]1.8 Release 0.4 Release Notes[/url] (TXT)
[/list]
So as you can see, a LOT has happened and we're still trucking along toward what will hopefully be an August release. Thanks so much for your patience and for wishlisting the game, it is much appreciated. Until next time!

notes.title: April, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.content:

notes.title: March, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.content:
Hey y'all, Brian here, and welcome to the March Star Fleet II development update. This was a pretty busy month, development-wise. Early in the month we got 1.6 Release 10, with new features to the CCC, improved mines, improved AI and much more, and release 10 got a bunch of patches to lead up to release 11, which dropped yesterday. Here are the details!

[list]
[*]1,6 Release 10 (3/6/21) - This release included improvements to both enemy and friendly AI, new features to the CCC like a navigation command, improved/more deadly mines along with more ways to avoid them, such as slowing down and coming to a stop. Release 10 received around half a dozen patches throughout the month to fix various problems that cropped up, such as speeding through a minefield if your target was another system, or planetary invasion zone selection problems. 
[*]1.6 Release 11 (3/30/21) - Much of the work leading up to Release 11 involved moving various functions to overlays so they take up less memory, and fixing more problems that cropped up as a result of issues with Release 10. As of this writing, it seems as if Release 11 is stable enough that Trevor can move forward working on the next major version of the game.
[/list]

I seriously hope that, in the next entry, I'll be able to tell you about 1.7. It apparently has some new features that will make admiral's lives much more challenging. Trevor says it's mere weeks away, and he's teasing us a LOT with new features that he won't specify. 

Finally, we moved our internal playtest version from being standalone now to Steam! This will definitely help make sure we're all using the exact same version as we test for bugs and come up with ideas for new features. 

I couldn't be more excited about how development is coming along, and I can't wait to bring you this game once it's ready! Thanks for reading y'all, and I'll see you both next month for another dev update and in the Monday Star Fleet II streams! Have a great one y'all!

notes.title: February, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.content:
Hey friends, 

Brian here! I hope you all had a lovely, joyous and safe February! Now, you might recall at the end of the last entry, we talked about the tentative release of 1.6 release 8. Each "release" is an iteration that builds upon and fixes issues with the previous release, while each numbered version (i.e 1.6, 1.7, etc) denotes major new features and such, just to clarify. 

Well, just as we were testing 1.6 release 8, we ran into some snags with it, and so much work was done with it that it eventually evolved into release 9.

[list]
[*]Release 9 (2/18/21) - This pretty big release includes fixes for mines, upgrades to the UGA AI (which is REALLY evident in higher-level missions), new commands (ALT-Y to go to the space forces table, for example), more information given about enemy starbases during an attack, improvements to escorts, improvements to the space forces table and a TON of other bug fixes.
[*]Release 10 (in pre-release) - The problem with a game with as many moving parts as Star Fleet II is when you fix some bugs, you seem to generate others. Our playtesters have been finding more, and Trevor has been squashing them, so the next release should have even more bug fixes and a few new features, which will be detailed once it's fully-released in the next dev update. 
[/list]

If you want to get an inkling as to how the sausage is made, you can read the [url=https://starfleet2.com/docs/SF2_V1_6_Notes_R9.pdf]full release notes PDF here[/url].

If you want to see a bunch of these changes and improvements in action (especially the more aggressive enemy AI, whoooboy), check out my latest stream.

[previewyoutube=Srq_jZUUpM4;full][/previewyoutube]

It's hoped that we'll hit 1.7 in March, which as you know brings us that much closer to 2.0. If you have time and interest and want to help us bring the game to Steam that much sooner, [url=https://starfleet2.com/contact/]please join our playtesting team[/url]! The more playtesters we have, the better! :)

That'll do it for this month's development update. Thanks so much to everyone who has wishlisted and followed us! We can't wait to bring 2.0 to you as soon as we all feel it's ready! :)

notes.title: January, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.content:
Hey friends, Brian Rubin/Space Game Junkie here, and welcome to our first monthly development update! This is something I figured we should do to keep y'all in the loop as to how development is progressing toward 2.0, so I'll whip this up on the last Friday of every month. I just thought of this a few days ago, so this entry will be a bit sketchy, but future entries should be...better. ;) With that said let's dive in. Keep in mind this is all for the current 1.6 branch:

[list]
[*]Release 4 (1/3/21) - This corrected starliner routes, fixed tables for space foces, properly denoted which planet you've entered orbit of, fixed exiting fleet command and added some bombardment features for escorts. It also added more fluid escort movement to make them seem more realistic as they move through space.
[*]Release 5 (1/11/21) - This added the hold fire all command, which is a very useful way for commanders at higher ranks (prefect and above) to stop firing on an enemy in case you need to get the kill shot or disable it. This also fixed memory problems.
[*]Release 6 (1/17/21) - This added laptop-friendly keys, added more functionality to the hold fire all command in the space forces table, and big news, added more layers to capturing an enemy starbase. Now a starbase needs its shields, torpedoes and phasers all knocked out before it's marked as disabled and ready for boarding. 
[*]Release 7 (1/24/21) - This fixed the never-ending space marines problem when trying to board a starbase. This also fixed memory problems, improved the notepad, and my favorite, added an indicator to the star systems table to denote which systems have enemy activity detected by your fleet.
[*]Release 8 (Tentatively 1/30/21) - We're testing this one right now (I got over an hour with it today), and it fixes some bugs we discovered with release 7, like some planets not being able to be scanned or not being able to set default speed. In my hour I spent making bases and killing UGA ships, I only had one issue which should hopefully be fixed soon (engine sounds cutting out). 
[/list]

So as you can see development is proceeding fairly rapidly. The hope is that release 8 of 1.6 is stable enough that Trevor can then move on and focus on adding new features for 1.7, which should hopefully drop in February. We'll keep you posted. Thanks for reading, and hail Zagar!

notes.title: 1.6 Released to Playesters
notes.content:
Friends, Brian Rubin here, to let you know that 1.6 -- the next major upgrade to the game -- has now been released to playtesters. This is a major milestone in the journey to us bringing it to Steam in the next few months. Many of the new features in 1.6 include:

[list]
[*]Tons of fixed bugs
[*]A new Fleet Management screen that allows you to easily see what all your other Krellan ships in the region are doing and where they are. 
[*]A new Combat Command Center that gives you quick and fluid control of the immediate battle area around your battlecruiser, including weapon, navigational and other commands.
[*]The ability to spend Krels to not only accelerate repair of crippled battlecruisers, but to upgrade your personal battlecruiser once you reach the rank of Subadmiral. This upgraded battlecruiser has, for example, more energy, armor, supplies, and shock troops. 
[*]Improved AI for both friendly and enemy forces.
[*]New defenses for the enemy, such as freighters which can now drop mines or ECM for heavy cruisers.
[*]Destroyers are now equipped with phasers alongside torpedoes to help combat upgrades to the UGA.
[*]Artifacts can now be found on planets and, if possible, installed on your ship for severe tactical upgrades.
[*]Troops on a planet will now call down dropships to withdraw from a conquered zone without your intervention.
[*]Easily navigate to any planet with new quick navigational features that will you to any planet, any planet with a landing party, or the closest friendly Starfort. 
[*]New Big Brother features, allowing you to tag planets vulnerable to a Big Brother takeover, as well as a status bar to keep track of how your landing parties are doing.
[*]And much more!
[/list]

1.6 is a massive revolutionary and evolutionary step up for the game, which will allow for even more to come in 1.7!

We can't wait to bring this to you once it hits 2.0. Thanks for all of you who have wishlisted the game, and we'll bring you more soon!

PS. If you would like to become a playtester, please contact us at [url=https://starfleet2.com/contact/]our website[/url]. Have a lovely holiday y'all, and Hail Zagar!

notes.title: Next Major Version Coming to Playtesters, Screenshots Released
notes.content:
Friends, the notes for the next major version of the game, 1.6, have just been released to playtesters, and it's a DOOZY. Some of the major new features include:

[h2]New Combat Control Center[/h2]

This new feature gives us a one-stop-shop for important controls while in the midst of combat, and it looks AMAZING.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/2d09e7db5f96c198d1f7e7016539ff60f21bafe5.png[/img] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/1e50234e604a30c499a0d2b35dd4d04fdc9d2504.png[/img]

When you reach the rank of Subadmiral, you have control over all friendly forces in the sector, and right now, to be honest, it's a bit clunky. This new fleet control system looks to really streamline controlling other ships, putting them into fleets and moving them where you need them. This will make coordinated attacks on things like enemy starbases so much more streamlined. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/7dbd839231d176a6e5d203e71fdff866f5d01286.png[/img]

We're also getting a ton of other new features such as:

[list]
[*]Upgraded escorts (they have phasers now!)
[*]Integrated notepad
[*]Quick navigation to specific planets, or planets with landing parties
[*]Use of in-game currency to repair or upgrade your personal battlecruiser
[*]Artifacts and experimental equipment
[/list]

And this is all just for version 1.6, which us playtesters hope to get by the end of the month, if not sooner. Future versions should have even more goodies to the leadup to 2.0!

If you'd like to be a playtester and help us get the game to Steam even sooner, plus play with all these new toys, be sure to contact Trevor Sorensen using our site's contact form!

https://starfleet2.com/contact/

We can't wait to not only get our hands on 1.6, but to eventually bring 2.0 to Steam with all these goodies, bug fixes and more! Thanks for reading y'all!
